question.:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}7 & -2 & 7 \\ 9 & -9 & 4 \\ -3 & 8 & 9\end{bmatrix}.
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation ${R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\begin{bmatrix}7 & -2 & 7 \\ 9 & -9 & 4 \\ -3 & 8 & 9\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}\leftrightarrow{R}_{3} \\ & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-3 & 8 & 9 \\ 9 & -9 & 4 \\ 7 & -2 & 7\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\begin{bmatrix}0 & 4 & 7 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-2{R}_{2} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}0+(-2)(5) & 4+(-2)(2) & 7+(-2)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}\quad {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(1)(5) & 3+(1)(2) & 0+(1)(1)\end{bmatrix} \\  & \sim \begin{bmatrix}-10 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 2 & 1 \\ 6 & 5 & 1\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$
